messages:
sara-nguyen: FYI I just saw an anomalous audit entry after the RBAC refactor deploy to staging. Looks like project-scoped roles are resolving to org scope in some cases.
leo-g: 😬 can you paste the audit line? which service?
sara-nguyen: sec-audit: action=access resource=project:acme-payments actor=user:bob@example.com resolved_scope=org:acme
ashok-r: that resolved_scope should be project:acme-payments not org:acme. which PR was the change? I saw scope normalization in #4821.
sec-bot: ALERT: rule=rbac_scope_mismatch count=1 first_seen=1724999950 severity=high
emily-ops: tagging incident triage. @jamie-plat can you grab runtime logs and KMS access checks? need to know if any key unwraps were allowed cross-project.
jamie-plat: on it. running quick query to find similar events.
jamie-plat: QUERY: select actor, resource, resolved_scope, timestamp from audit_events where rule='rbac_scope_mismatch' and timestamp > 1724990000 limit 50;
jamie-plat: results show 8 hits across 3 orgs. objects accessed look like model endpoints and bucket metadata, not KMS decrypt calls so far.
sara-nguyen: ok good about KMS. still bad. can we force a rollback of the scope-change toggle in staging and prod toggles if present?
leo-g: I pushed a hotfix branch (fix/rbac-scope-check) that tightens scope precedence. can roll to prod but want to confirm blast radius.
ashok-r: mitigation plan: 1) flip rollout flag to previous behavior 2) run audit query for unusual accesses since 1724995000 3) rotate any short-lived credentials if necessary 4) notify affected customers if data exposure probable
emily-ops: executing 1 now: dashboard shows flag disabled at 1725000200. will watch for new mismatches.
jamie-plat: running audit replay to enumerate resources accessed with resolved_scope != intended_scope. cmd: `./tools/audit-find --since 1724995000 --mismatch` output -> /tmp/rbac-mismatch-172500
sara-nguyen: copying results to sec-sleuth. initial glance: one read of project config for customer acme-corp by actor in sibling project. Need to confirm whether that read included secrets or only metadata.
leo-g: I grep'd the raw request payload; it's GET /v1/projects/acme-corp/config -> response contains env vars but no KMS plaintext. KMS unwrap logs show no decrypt for those keys. so data exposure likely limited to config names and non-secret fields.
legal-eng: flagging compliance. keep logs and timeline. if any PII present we escalate.
sara-nguyen: thanks. next steps: 1) leave flag off in prod 2) ship fix to master with unit+integration tests for scope resolution 3) run customer-impact report and prepare notification template if needed.
ashok-r: I'll prepare a postmortem draft after we confirm full extent. can someone add the list of affected resources to the incident doc?
jamie-plat: uploaded /tmp/rbac-mismatch-172500 -> drive and added to incident doc. linking: https://drive.company/internal/rbac-172500
sec-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation=rollback flag disabled at 1725000200, active_hits=0 in last 10m
sara-nguyen: good job. will schedule a brief on-call sync in 15 to review patch rollout path and test matrix. anyone object to a short customer notif if we find more than 1 customer with config reads?
legal-eng: we'll advise on wording; hold until we confirm no secrets were exposed.
leo-g: I'll open PR with tests and request expedited review. ping me in thread if you need me to push emergency patch to prod.
ashok-r: assigning follow-ups: leo PR, jamie resource list, emily notify ops runbook, sara postmortem lead.
sara-nguyen: thanks all. closing loop after patch lands and a 24h audit sweep.
